sections.h2: Which Pettis County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two courthouse offices split the work and a third records the deed. The assessor values property. The collector mails the bill and takes payment. Both are at 415 S Ohio in Sedalia, MO 65301, and both answer through the county switchboard at 660-826-5000.

  • Assessor: Suite 218, extension 920, fax 660-829-2492, wooleryc@pettiscomo.com
  • Collector: second floor, Suite 216, extension 921, fax 660-826-6254, pettiscollector@pettiscomo.com, open 8:00 am to 5:00 pm weekdays except holidays
  • Recorder of Deeds: Suite 106, extension 922

The assessor does not set tax rates or district budgets. Schools, cities, fire districts and other districts set their own rates, and the collector collects whatever amount is assigned to each owner.

sections.h2: How a Pettis County house is valued
sections.html:
Real estate is revalued in odd-numbered years. A value set as of that January 1 stays on the books through the following even year, and only new construction or demolition changes it in between. The assessor looks at sales of comparable properties, the condition and physical features of the home, and any building or teardown work.

Fixed percentages turn market value into assessed value:

  • Homes and other residential land: 19 percent
  • Farmland: 12 percent
  • Commercial parcels: 32 percent

Each district's levy is then applied to every $100 of assessed value to produce the bill. RSMo 137.115 backs the percentages. It also stops the assessor from raising a residential parcel by more than 15 percent without a physical inspection, unless the jump comes from new construction.

The assessor describes three stages. The first is a sit-down at the assessor's office to learn how your number was built and what records support it. Many disputes end right there.

  1. Call the assessor soon after the valuation notice arrives and ask for a meeting.
  2. If that fails, the county clerk provides forms and deadlines for the Board of Equalization, which hears the assessor and then you.
  3. Still unhappy? The State Tax Commission accepts appeals until September 30 or thirty days after the board's last action, whichever is later.

Two state rules favor the owner. A value increase must be reported to the record owner, with the statute setting June 15 as the mailing date (RSMo 137.180). At the board, no one presumes the assessor is right, and if a parcel's assessed value rose 15 percent or more, new construction aside, the assessor carries the burden of proof (RSMo 138.060). The commission route appears in RSMo 138.430.

sections.h2: Due date and ways to pay
sections.html:
December 31 is the date that counts. Money not received by then draws penalties and fees. Card and phone payments clear slowly, so pay well before midnight on the last day.

Pettis County payment options
Payment optionCostSpeed

Same website, e-checkFreeAround ten days to clear
Phone line 877-690-3729 (enter code 3526, then the account or parcel number)Confirm when you callSlow to post
Suite 216 counter in personNo online card feeReceipt in hand at the counter

The county keeps none of the card fee, and the office itself takes no payments by phone. Mailed receipts take about a week to ten days. A vehicle owner who needs proof of payment for a license renewal late in the month should pay at the office.

Vehicles, livestock, farm machinery and business equipment are taxed in the county where the owner lived on January 1. The assessor mails forms in January, and a declaration filed by March 1 avoids late assessment penalties. Vehicles and most equipment are assessed at 33 and one third percent of value, farm equipment and livestock at 12 percent, and a vehicle with historic plates at 5 percent.

Someone moving to Pettis County from another state brings registration papers or titles to the assessor's office to open an account. A person who was not a Missouri resident on January 1 is exempt for that first year and can get a statement of no tax due. Movers within Missouri need proper tax papers from the county where they lived on the prior January 1.

Pettis County has adopted the Senate Bill 190 program, which gives an eligible senior a credit on the real estate tax bill of a primary residence. The county's FAQ lists the main conditions:

  • The applicant lives in Pettis County and turned 62 before January 1 of the first credit year.
  • The applicant owns or holds a recorded interest in the home and is liable for its real estate taxes.
  • The home is the primary residence, lived in 183 days or more a year, and assessed as residential.
  • Rental portions, bed and breakfast space and short term rental areas do not qualify.

The credit equals the difference between the tax owed and what the home owed in the base year. It appears on the statement and is not a refund, and it does not reach back before the base year. Applications and each renewal must be signed before a notary or collector staff. The application window opens in spring, so ask the collector in Suite 216 for the current dates. Skip a renewal and the program ends, which forces a new base year.

Call the collector at 660-826-5000 ext 921 before you list and ask for the balance on your account, any earlier year included. The collector finds accounts by account number or by the name on the tax statement, so keep the bill handy. Ask the title company to show that balance as a line on the settlement statement.

Online and phone payments post slowly, so a payoff in the final days before closing is best made at the courthouse counter in Suite 216. If your mailing address has changed, tell the assessor in Suite 218 so notices reach you. A cash buyer can close on a short timeline, and the payoff still comes from your proceeds at the table, so get the balance in writing early rather than on closing morning.

Sedalia anchors a county of roughly 682 square miles in west central Missouri, with small towns such as Green Ridge, Houstonia, Hughesville, Ionia, La Monte, Smithton and Windsor around it. The July 2025 population estimate is 44,254 across 18,953 housing units, and 117 building permits were issued in 2025. Typical monthly owner costs run $1,211 with a mortgage and $444 without one. Bills include levies for whichever school district covers the parcel, among them Sedalia 200, Pettis County R-V, Green Ridge R-VIII, La Monte R-IV and Smithton.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Pettis County real estate tax?
faqs.a: December 31. Payments not received by then draw late penalties and fees, so allow time for online and phone payments to process.

faqs.q: What assessment rates apply to Pettis County property?
faqs.a: Residential property is assessed at 19 percent of market value, agricultural at 12 percent and commercial at 32 percent.

faqs.q: Where does a valuation dispute go?
faqs.a: Meet with the assessor first, then go to the county Board of Equalization through the county clerk, and last to the State Tax Commission. The commission deadline is the later of September 30 or 30 days after the board's final action.
Card payments carry a fee of at least $1.55 or 2.45 percent, which the county does not keep. E-checks have no fee but need about ten days to clear.

faqs.q: Does Pettis County offer tax relief to seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. The county runs the Senate Bill 190 credit for residents 62 and older on a primary residence. Ask the collector when the next application window opens.
